title: Harden auth stack and rotate crypto/SAML transitive deps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Replace and remediate several vulnerable transitive dependencies in the authentication stack. Scope includes OpenSSL-linked modules in the Go runtime, Node JWT libraries used by the API gateway, and the SAML SSO connector (onelogin/ssoconnector) used by the Console. The work will standardize on vetted library versions, remove deprecated TLS APIs, centralize JWT verification logic, and rotate in-memory crypto config so deployments do not rely on old primitives. This ticket is the engineering remediation track coordinated with Security and SRE: patch, test, and roll out with a controlled canary and emergency rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: All identified high/critical CVEs removed from dependency tree (no remaining vulnerable OpenSSL consumers)
CI gates include new SBOM and vulnerability scan reports with zero critical findings for prod services
Auth middleware (Go) uses the updated TLS config abstraction and passes interop tests with legacy clients
Node gateway JWT verification migrated to centralized service with feature flag and integration tests
SAML connector upgraded and verified against IdP testbed; end-to-end login flows pass manual smoke tests
Rollout completed to 10% canary, 50% mid, and 100% once metrics are stable; rollback plan rehearsed
implementation_notes: Inventory: used `go list -m all`, `npm audit` and `pipdeptree` to find transitive OpenSSL/JWT/SAML consumers (doc: confluence/infra/auth-dep-inventory)
Target versions: OpenSSL consumers pinned to libs linking OpenSSL >= 3.1.1 where possible; node jsonwebtoken replaced with maintained fork (jsonwebtoken-maintained v9.0.0) for CVE fixes
Go changes: migrate tls.Config usage to auth/tlswrapper with explicit MinVersion and Curve selection; remove calls to DeprecatedCipherSuiteSet
Node changes: extract JWT verification into /services/auth-verifier to enforce consistent leeway, key rotation handling, and jwks caching
SAML: upgrade onelogin/ssoconnector to v3.4.0, apply a small patch for XML canonicalization edge case (attached PR patch), add parsing hardening
Builds: regenerate SBOMs and rebuild minimal runtime images; add linker flags to ensure new OpenSSL symbols included
Coordination: Security review required before canary; notify SRE to schedule canary window and extra alerting
rollout_plan: Deploy changes to staging and run synthetic auth scenarios for 48 hours. Deploy to prod canary subset (10%) during low-traffic window; monitor latency, 4xx/5xx auth errors, token rejection rate, CPU for crypto ops, and SRE alerts. If stable for 24h, advance to 50% then 100% over 48-72h. Feature flags allow fallback to old verifier for traffic slices. Post-rollout, run full smoke regression and update SBOM in release artifacts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for new TLS wrapper and jwt verifier with key rotation simulation
Integration tests between API gateway, auth-verifier, and console with mocked JWKS and IdP SAML testbed
Fuzz testing for SAML XML input and JWT header/parsing edge cases
Performance bench for token verification latency at 1k RPS to ensure CPU impact acceptable
Staging canary run with production-like dataset and automated rollback triggers on auth error spike
rollback_plan: Use feature flag to switch traffic back to previous verifier; if flag fails, roll back container revision via deployment controller to previous image. In parallel, revoke any rotated keys if compromise suspected and trigger incident response runbook.
